parole.significato: A South American freshwater river fish, Hoplias aimara.
parole.testo: From a native name; said by Century to be Tupi, but perhaps in fact Cariban: contrast Emerillon taɾeʔiɾ (“aïmara”) with Trió aimara (“anjumara”).

parole.significato: A tropical American evergreen shrub, Bixa orellana; the lipstick tree; the fruit of the tree.

A Brazilian plant, the cricket-vine (Fridericia chica).
parole.testo: Ultimately from a Cariban or Tupi-Guarani language; compare Ye'kwana küdayü, possessed form küdayüdü, Kari'na karawiru, Pemon karaweru, Wayampi karayuru.

parole.significato: A chigoe (Tunga penetrans), a kind of flea found in tropical climates.
parole.testo: From chigoe, likely from a Cariban language term such as Kari'na siko (“chigoe”) (early recorded variant chico), from Proto-Cariban *tikô.

parole.significato: A plant, Strychnos toxifera, formerly used in arrow poisons in South America due to its D-tubocurarine content.
parole.testo: From a Cariban language; compare Kari'na urari, Trió urari, wïrari, Akawaio urari, Pemon urari, Macushi urari, referring to various vines of genus Strychnos.

parole.significato: A destructive possessing spirit according to the beliefs of parts of South America.
parole.testo: Borrowed from various Cariban sources such as Ye'kwana kanaimö, Kari'na kanaimo, Pemon kanaimö.

parole.significato: A shaman among the indigenous peoples of Guyana.
parole.testo: From a Cariban language, ultimately from Proto-Cariban *pɨjati; compare Kari'na pyjai, Trió pïjai, Akurio piyahi, Wayana pïjai, Yao (South America) peeiai (“shaman”).

parole.significato: A shaman among the indigenous peoples of Guyana.
parole.testo: From a Cariban language, ultimately from Proto-Cariban *pɨjati; compare Trió pïjai, Akurio piyahi, Carijona hiyači (“shaman”) (from Proto-Taranoan *pɨjaci, from the Proto-Cariban term).

parole.significato: Albizia saman, a large tropical tree in the pea family.
